units.text: Aspose.Email FOSS for .Net reads and writes MSG and EML email formats, and inspects CFB container structures. It converts EML messages to MSG format and back, and loads MSG files from streams or saves them to streams. It reads sector size and directory entry information from CFB files such as MSG containers.
It reads Outlook MSG files from streams or files using MapiMessage.FromStream and writes them back with Save, preserving MAPI property streams, recipient storages, and attachment sub-storages.
It creates new messages in memory with MapiMessage.Create, sets SenderName and SenderEmailAddress, adds recipients with AddRecipient, and attaches files with AddAttachment before saving to disk.
It converts EML files to MSG using MapiMessage.LoadFromEml and back to EML using SaveToEml, implementing native MIME parsing and serialization without external dependencies.

It opens Compound File Binary containers with CfbReader.FromFile, exposes sector size and directory entry count, and iterates the internal tree structure with IterTree to inspect nested storages and streams.
It reads and writes arbitrary MAPI properties on messages using SetProperty and GetPropertyValue, beyond the strongly-typed properties MapiMessage exposes directly.
It adds recipients with AddRecipient and attaches files or nested embedded messages with AddAttachment and AddEmbeddedMessageAttachment, supporting both external files and in-memory content.
This example reads a MSG file and prints its subject line using Aspose.Email.Foss version 26.7.0 targeting net8.0.
Create and save an MSG message, convert EML to MSG, and inspect a CFB container's structure.
Create and save an MSG message with sender, recipient, and attachment.
Convert an EML file to MSG and back to EML.
Inspect the CFB structure of a MSG file.

Aspose.Email FOSS for .Net provides high-level message handling through MapiMessage and lower-level access via CfbReader/CfbWriter and MsgReader/MsgWriter/MsgDocument, supporting the net8.0 target framework in version 0.1.0 of the package.

The Aspose.Email FOSS for .Net public symbol exposes MapiMessage as the primary entry point for creating, editing, and converting messages, while CfbReader/CfbWriter and MsgReader/MsgWriter/MsgDocument provide direct lower-level access to the Aspose.Email.Foss.Cfb and Aspose.Email.Foss.Msg namespaces.
The getting started guide covers installation, walkthroughs, and feature guides for this library.
The how-to guides and FAQ provide task-focused answers for common MSG, CFB, and EML questions.
The full API reference offers the complete, browsable reference for all 29 public types.
The public API summary lists the repository's own stable-namespace and primary-type list.
The changelog documents the release history.
Users can open an issue on GitHub to report bugs or request features.
Aspose.Email FOSS for .Net reads and writes local email files in formats supported by the Aspose.Email.Foss package version 26.7.0 for the net8.0 target framework.
The package does not support IMAP, SMTP, or POP3 protocols and works only with local files, not mail servers.
Transport Neutral Encapsulation Format files are not parsed or generated.
Calendar or appointment support is not provided; calendar-specific MAPI properties can be accessed generically via SetProperty() or GetPropertyValue() only.
The package requires the .NET 8.0 SDK (or later) to build and the matching .NET 8.0 runtime (or later) to run; classic .NET Framework (4.x) is not supported.

Aspose.Email FOSS for .Net targets net8.0 and builds using the .NET CLI. The main library project has no external package dependencies; CFB, MSG, and EML/MIME handling are implemented natively. Test dependencies — Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.8.0, xunit 2.5.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 2.5.3, and coverlet.collector 6.0.0 — apply only to the test project under tests/ and are not shipped with the package. Clone the repository and run the xUnit test suite to verify CFB round-trips, MSG reading, and EML round-trip conversion, or run one of the example programs under examples/.

it adds broader format and protocol coverage: direct IMAP/SMTP/POP3 mail-server connectivity, TNEF (winmail.dat) support, calendar and appointment APIs, and classic .NET Framework support alongside this edition's MSG, CFB, and EML processing.
CfbConstants provides constant values used in Compound File Binary format processing.
CfbDocument represents a Compound File Binary structure and provides methods to load it from files, streams, or readers.
CfbException represents errors that occur during Compound File Binary format processing.
CfbNode represents a node in a Compound File Binary structure with properties such as name, class identifier, timestamps, and state bits.
CfbReader provides functionality to read and navigate a Compound File Binary structure, including accessing directory entries, streams, and storage nodes.
CfbStorage represents a storage node in a Compound File Binary structure that can contain child storages and streams.
CfbStream represents a stream node in a Compound File Binary structure that holds binary data.
CfbWriter provides functionality to write a Compound File Binary structure.
DirectoryEntry represents an entry in the directory of a Compound File Binary structure.
DirectoryEntryNameComparer provides a comparer for directory entries based on their names.
Header represents the header information of a Compound File Binary structure.
MapiAttachment represents an attachment in a MAPI message.
MapiMessage represents a MAPI message and provides access to its properties, recipients, and attachments.
MapiProperty represents a single property in a MAPI message.
MapiPropertyCollection represents a collection of MAPI properties.
MapiRecipient represents a recipient in a MAPI message.
MsgConstants provides constant values used in MSG format processing.
MsgDocument represents an MSG format file and provides methods to load it from files, streams, or readers.
MsgException represents errors that occur during MSG format processing.
MsgReader provides functionality to read and navigate an MSG format file.
MsgStorage represents a storage node in an MSG format file.
MsgStorageRole specifies the role of a storage node in an MSG format file.
MsgStream represents a stream node in an MSG format file.
MsgWriter provides functionality to write an MSG format file.
